newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho profit falls, sees split-up advance.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho profit falls, sees split-up advance.

text.p: Mining-to hotels conglomerate Lonrho on Monday reported a fall in first-half profits and said it expected to make good progress this year in hiving off its African trading business.
Lonrho, which is in preliminary merger talks with South African mining group JCI Ltd, saw pre-tax profit drop to 38 million pounds ($62.9 million) from 61 million.
Lonrho, which announced its merger talks with JCI last month, made no comments on the present state of negotiations.
But Lonrho did say it was in continuing talks to sell its Princess Hotels, while adding that the planned separation of Lonrho Africa was a complex process.
"But we anticipate that it will be well advanced by the end of the calendar year," Lonrho said.
The group's profits, which met analysts' expectations, were hit by the pound's strength and lower contributions from Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields Co Ltd, Lonrho said.
Poor precious metal prices and moderate trading in the African business also weighed on profits.
The overall group results excluded a 129 million pound net profit on disposal of Lonrho Sugar earlier this year. ($ = 0.604 British Pounds)
